one_line_reason: The clearest human signals for hops are a combination sleep trial (valerian+hops) and a narrative (non-quantified) review of hop iso-alpha-acids on metabolic markers; neither is clean single-ingredient quantified evidence.

selected.intervention: Valerian-hops extract combination (Ze 91019), oral, 21-day treatment period vs placebo
selected.primary_outcome: sleep duration (via Fitbit tracker); secondary daytime cognitive and psychological measures
selected.why_selected: The only shortlisted RCT directly testing the classic hops-for-sleep marketing claim, with a statistically significant increase in sleep duration, though only as a feasibility trial and only as a valerian-hops combination

selected.population: human interventional trial subjects (exact populations not specified in this review-level abstract)
selected.intervention: Humulus lupulus iso-α-acids (bitter hop acids), oral, across multiple cited human interventional trials
selected.primary_outcome: weight, lipid metabolism, glucose homeostasis, insulin sensitivity, inflammation
selected.why_selected: A hops-specific (not multi-plant-pooled) systematic review summarizing multiple human interventional trials as showing beneficial metabolic effects, though it is a narrative synthesis without a single pooled effect size in the abstract

blockers: 40462685 tests a fixed valerian+hops combination product (Ze 91019), not hops alone, and is explicitly framed as a feasibility trial with only exploratory statistical significance

33670177 is a narrative systematic review of iso-α-acids specifically (a purified bitter-acid fraction of hops), not whole hop extract, and does not report a single quantified effect size or individual trial dose/population details in the abstract
The two xanthohumol RCTs in the shortlist are in Crohn's disease patients with safety/tolerability as the primary outcome, not general-population efficacy

handoff_pmids.note: Phase 2 safety and tolerability trial of xanthohumol (a hop flavonoid) 24 mg/day in adults with Crohn's disease; primary outcomes are toxicology labs, vital signs, and adverse events, not efficacy

excluded_pmids.reason: Companion trial to 41834265 (XMaS trial) in Crohn's disease patients, exploring xanthohumol's effect on gut microbiome/bile-acid metabolism; mechanistic/exploratory in a clinical IBD population, not a general-use health-outcome efficacy trial

Reviews phytoestrogens broadly (soy, red clover, red grapes, hops, flaxseed, black cohosh); the detailed efficacy discussion in the retrieved abstract centers on soy isoflavones and resveratrol, not hops specifically
Reviews many phytoestrogens (Pueraria mirifica, fennel, hops, soy, red clover, black cohosh, etc.) pooled together for urogenital menopause symptoms; hops-specific data is not isolated
Systematic review of plants modulating the HPA axis; the plants named in the retrieved abstract (ashwagandha, ginseng, St John's Wort, CBD, Rhodiola, curcumin, etc.) do not include hops
Systematic review of GABA-modulating anxiolytic phytomedicines; hops is not named among the plants discussed in the retrieved abstract text
Comparative genomics study of Cannabis and Humulus (hops); a plant-genomics analysis, not a human health trial
Position paper on oncology pharmacy practice; unrelated to hops, evidently a mismatched retrieval
Study of impact/resistance exercise on bone/cartilage biomarkers; 'hops' here refers to jumping movements in the exercise protocol, not the herb Humulus lupulus
Forefoot strengthening and athletic performance study; 'hops' refers to foot-ankle jumping movements in the exercise testing, not the herb
